standard_text: Understand the integer number system; recognize opposite signs of numbers as locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; understand that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself.

progression.narrative: 6.NS.2 asks students to understand the integer number system through the idea of OPPOSITES: numbers with opposite signs live on opposite sides of 0 on the number line, and taking the opposite of the opposite returns the original number. The logic starts on the number line itself. First a student has to SEE opposites as mirror twins across 0 -- opposite signs AND equal distance (S1), because a plotted point makes both checks countable. Then the picture goes away: from a distance and direction alone ('7 units left of 0'), the student names the number and its opposite (S2) -- the first place distance (always positive) and the signed number get pried apart. The idea then generalizes to every rational number: the opposite of a decimal or fraction changes only the sign, never the digits (S3), which is where 'opposite' must be defended against 'reciprocal.' With the mechanics solid, the student puts the relationship into words -- same distance, opposite sides, for any pair (S4), confronting the belief that a negative number is 'closer to 0 because it's smaller.' Finally the standard's capstone: an opposite is an ACTION (a flip across 0), so the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, even when the number is a variable (S5).

steps.rationale: Opposites begin as a picture: mirror twins across 0. A plotted point lets the student count both checks -- opposite sides AND equal distance -- before any notation carries the load.
The standard says opposite signs indicate LOCATIONS. From 'N units left/right of 0' the student names the signed number and its opposite -- the first place distance and value must be kept separate.

The integer idea extends to all rational numbers: the opposite of a decimal or fraction changes only the sign. Here 'opposite' must be distinguished from 'reciprocal' before both words are needed later.
Understanding means saying it: any pair -N and N sits the same distance from 0 in opposite directions. This step dismantles 'smaller means closer to 0' -- the value-versus-distance confusion.

The standard's final clause: the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself. Treating each sign as a flip across 0 -- including for variables like -(-n) -- is the capstone of the progression.

skills.name: Locate and read integers on a number line

prerequisite_skill.description: Place and read whole numbers on a number line, with numbers growing to the right
prerequisite_skill.check_question: On a number line, which direction do numbers get bigger -- left or right?

skills.i_do_script: We're going to read a number line that has numbers on BOTH sides of 0. Point at 0 with me -- that's home base. Watch: I count 4 ticks to the LEFT of 0 and land on -4. The negative sign just means 'left of 0.' I never start counting from the end of the line -- always from 0.

canonical_error.pattern: Reads a point by its distance only, dropping the negative sign for points left of 0
canonical_error.example: A point 3 ticks to the left of 0 is read as '3' instead of '-3'
canonical_error.why: The student's number-line experience is whole numbers only, so 'how far' is the whole answer. They haven't attached direction (which side of 0) to the number's sign.

skills.item_template: A short prompt naming a distance and direction from 0, or asking which side of 0 a number sits on. NR or one-word response -- no choices, built for fluency sprints.

sample_items.stem: What number is 4 units left of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 4 -- student gives the distance and drops the sign

sample_items.stem: What number is 7 units right of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: -7 -- student attaches a sign out of habit once negatives appear

sample_items.stem: Is -5 left or right of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Right -- student ignores the negative sign

sample_items.stem: Is 3 left or right of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Left -- student is guessing rather than using the sign

sample_items.stem: What number is 1 unit left of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 1 -- distance without direction

sample_items.stem: What number is 0 units from 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Student may freeze -- 0 is neither left nor right of itself

sample_items.stem: Which is farther left: -2 or -6?
sample_items.distractor_logic: -2 -- student thinks the 'smaller-looking' digit is farther left

sample_items.stem: Which is farther right: 4 or 1?
sample_items.distractor_logic: 1 -- student confuses closer-to-0 with farther right

sample_items.stem: What number is 8 units left of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 8 -- drops the sign

sample_items.stem: What number is 2 units right of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: -2 -- sign attached to the wrong direction

sample_items.stem: Is -1 left or right of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Right -- student ignores the small negative

sample_items.stem: What number is 6 units left of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 6 -- distance without direction

sample_items.stem: Which is farther left: -3 or -7?
sample_items.distractor_logic: -3 -- student reads 3 < 7 and picks the smaller digit

sample_items.stem: What number is 5 units right of 0?
sample_items.distractor_logic: -5 -- sign added where none belongs

redirect_script.stop: Pause -- where is 0 on this line?
redirect_script.prompt: Put your finger on 0 first. Now count the ticks TO the point. Which direction did your finger move -- left or right? Left of 0 means the number wears a negative sign.
redirect_script.praise: You started at 0 and used the direction. That's exactly how integers work.

vocabulary.definition: A straight line with 0 in the middle, positive numbers to the right, and negative numbers to the left.
A whole number, its negative, or zero -- like -3, 0, and 7.
A number less than 0. It lives to the LEFT of 0 on the number line.

next_steps.if_pass: Move to 6NS2-F2: connect negative numbers to real situations like temperature and elevation, then start 6NS2-S1.
next_steps.if_fail: Practice counting ticks from 0 on a drawn line, left and right, with the student saying the direction out loud each time. Repeat this bank next session.

worked_example_script.text: Draw a number line from -8 to 8 and circle the 0. Say: '0 is home base -- everything gets counted from here.'
Which direction do numbers get bigger on this line? Which direction do they get smaller?
Put your finger on 0 and hop 4 ticks to the left. Land and pause.
How many ticks did I move, and which direction? So what number is this?
If the student says '4,' they counted distance but dropped the direction. Ask: 'Is this spot on the bigger side of 0 or the smaller side? What mark does a number wear when it's LEFT of 0?'
Now you try: start at 0 and find the number 6 units to the right. What is it? Does it need a negative sign? Why not?
Last one: which is farther left, -2 or -6? Prove it by pointing at both on the line.
Every integer is just two pieces of information: how far from 0, and which side. Keep saying both pieces out loud until it's automatic.

printable_artifact.title: Reading Integers From 0 Quick Reference
printable_artifact.instructions: Keep this nearby. Always start at 0, then count and say the direction.
items: Start counting at 0, never at the end of the line
Farther left = smaller; farther right = bigger

skills.name: Recognize that negative numbers describe values below zero

prerequisite_skill.description: Understand 0 as a reference point (sea level, zero degrees, ground floor)
prerequisite_skill.check_question: If the temperature is 0 degrees and it gets colder, what happens to the number on the thermometer?

skills.i_do_script: Numbers below zero show up in real life all the time -- temperatures below freezing, divers below sea level, money you owe. Watch: a diver 12 feet BELOW sea level is at -12 feet. The word 'below' is my clue that the number is negative. Sea level itself is 0.

canonical_error.pattern: Drops the negative sign when writing a below-zero quantity
canonical_error.example: Writes '5' for a temperature of 5 degrees below zero instead of '-5'
canonical_error.why: The student treats the sign as optional decoration. They record the SIZE of the quantity but not its position relative to zero, because in earlier grades every quantity was above zero.

skills.item_template: A one-sentence real-world situation (temperature, elevation, money) involving a value above, below, or at zero. Student writes the signed number. NR response.

sample_items.stem: The temperature is 7 degrees below zero. Write this temperature as a number.
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 7 -- the sign is dropped because 'below' is not connected to negative

sample_items.stem: A diver is 12 feet below sea level. What number shows the diver's position?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 12 -- position and depth are confused

sample_items.stem: Marcus owes his brother 4 dollars. What number shows the change in Marcus's money?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 4 -- owing is not recognized as a below-zero amount

sample_items.stem: An elevator stops 2 levels below the ground floor. What number names that level?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 2 -- 'below ground' not linked to a negative

sample_items.stem: Which temperature is below zero: -6 degrees or 6 degrees?
sample_items.distractor_logic: 6 degrees -- student ignores the sign and compares digits

sample_items.stem: A football team loses 9 yards on a play. What number shows the change in yards?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 9 -- a loss is written as a gain

sample_items.stem: Sea level is written as what number?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Student may leave it blank -- 0 as a reference point is unfamiliar

sample_items.stem: A hawk flies 15 feet above sea level. What number shows its position?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: -15 -- student over-applies the negative sign once negatives appear

redirect_script.stop: Hold on -- is this amount above zero or below zero?
redirect_script.prompt: Circle the direction word in the sentence: 'below,' 'under,' 'owes,' 'loses' all mean BELOW zero, so the number wears a negative sign. 'Above' and 'gains' mean positive. Rewrite your number with the right sign.
redirect_script.praise: You matched the direction word to the sign. That's what the negative sign is for.

vocabulary.definition: A number below zero, written with a - sign, like -7.
A number above zero. It can be written with or without a + sign.
The reference point -- sea level, zero degrees, the ground floor. Zero is neither positive nor negative.

next_steps.if_pass: Move to 6NS2-S1: find opposite numbers on the number line.
next_steps.if_fail: Go back to 6NS2-F1 and rebuild the left-of-0 idea on a drawn number line, then retry these contexts with a vertical thermometer picture.

worked_example_script.text: Write on the board: 'A diver is 12 feet below sea level.' Draw a quick vertical line with 0 labeled 'sea level.'
Where is sea level on our picture? What number does sea level get?
Is the diver above the 0 line or below it? Which word in the sentence told you?
If below zero means negative, what number shows the diver's position?
If the student writes 12, don't correct it directly. Ask: 'Where would a bird 12 feet ABOVE sea level be? Should the bird and the diver get the same number?' Let the collision force the sign.
Now try one alone: the temperature is 7 degrees below zero. What number is that? Which word was your clue?
Whenever a situation goes below zero -- colder, deeper, owing -- the number wears a negative sign. The sign IS the direction.

printable_artifact.title: Above Zero or Below Zero Sort
printable_artifact.instructions: Cut apart the cards. Sort each situation under 'Above zero (+)', 'Below zero (-)', or 'Exactly zero (0)'.
items: a diver 30 feet under the sea

skills.name: Identify opposite numbers on a number line
skills.i_do_script: Opposites are mirror twins across 0. Watch me check whether -5 and 5 are opposites: I count -5's distance from 0 -- five units, on the left. Then 5's distance -- five units, on the right. Same distance, opposite sides: they're opposites. Two points are NOT opposites just because one is negative and one is positive -- the distances have to match.

canonical_error.pattern: Calls any negative-positive pair 'opposites' without checking that both are the same distance from 0
canonical_error.example: Says -3 and 5 are opposites because one is negative and one is positive
canonical_error.why: The student attends only to the signs. They haven't internalized that 'opposite' means a mirror image across 0 -- opposite signs AND equal distance from 0.

skills.item_template: A number line from -8 to 8 with labeled points. Student picks the pair of points that are opposites, or names the opposite of one marked point. MC with 4 choices; a figure is always shown.

sample_items.stem:
A number line is given. Each point represents a value.

Which pair of points represent opposite values?
choices: J and N
K and M
L and N
J and K
sample_items.distractor_logic: K and M (-2 and 3) baits the signs-only error: opposite signs but different distances from 0. L and N share a side of 0's distance mismatch; J and K are both negative.

sample_items.stem:
A number line is given. Each point represents a value.

Which pair of points represent opposite values?
choices: K and M
J and N
L and M
K and N
sample_items.distractor_logic: J and N (-7 and 6) look symmetric but are unequal distances from 0 -- the signs-only bait. L and M sit on the same side; K and N mix -3 with 6.

sample_items.stem:
A number line is given. Point M represents a value.

What is the opposite of the number located at Point M?
sample_items.distractor_logic: -4 is the number itself (no flip); 0 is the mirror point misread as the answer; -8 doubles the distance instead of crossing 0.

sample_items.stem:
A number line is given. Point P represents a value.

What is the opposite of the number located at Point P?
sample_items.distractor_logic: 6 is the number itself; 0 is the center misread as the opposite; 12 doubles the value instead of reflecting it.

redirect_script.stop: Wait -- did you check the distances?
redirect_script.prompt: Opposites need TWO things: opposite sides of 0 AND the same distance from 0. Count each point's ticks from 0 out loud. Do the counts match?
redirect_script.praise: You checked both the side and the distance. That's the whole definition of opposites.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers the same distance from 0 but on opposite sides, like -5 and 5.
How many units a number is away from 0, counted without worrying about direction.
The + or - that tells which side of 0 a number is on.

skills.manipulative_visual: Fold a paper number line exactly at 0. Opposites land on top of each other when the paper is folded. Let the student fold to CHECK every answer before trusting it.

next_steps.if_pass: Move to 6NS2-S2: name a number and its opposite from a distance and direction, without a picture.
next_steps.if_fail: Check 6NS2-F1 -- can the student read a point left of 0 correctly? If yes, re-run S1 with the paper-folding check until 'same distance' becomes automatic.

worked_example_script.text: Draw a number line from -8 to 8. Plot and label points: J at -5, K at -2, L at 1, M at 3, N at 5.
We're hunting for a pair of OPPOSITE points. Before we hunt -- what two things have to be true for two numbers to be opposites?
Look at K at -2 and M at 3. One is negative and one is positive. Are they opposites? Count each one's distance from 0.
If the student says K and M are opposites, they're using signs only. Have them count ticks: K is 2 from 0, M is 3 from 0. Ask: 'Do the distances match? Then can they be mirror twins?'
Now check J at -5. How far is J from 0? Which point on the RIGHT side is exactly that far from 0?
So which pair is the true opposite pair? Say the two checks that prove it.
Fold the number line at 0 (or draw a mirror arrow over the top). Show J landing exactly on N.
That's the test you'll run every time: opposite sides of 0, same distance from 0. Both checks, every time.

printable_artifact.title: Opposite Pairs Reference Card
printable_artifact.instructions: Opposites are mirror twins across 0. Use the two-check test on every pair.

practice_problems.stem: Point A is on the number line shown. What is the opposite of the number at Point A?
practice_problems.notes: Small numbers, figure given -- just run the two-check test.

practice_problems.stem: Mark the point that is the opposite of 3 on the number line.
Points A, B, C, D, and E are shown on the number line. Which pair of points shows opposite values?
practice_problems.notes: B and D (-1 and 4) is the signs-only trap -- listen for whether the student counts distances.

practice_problems.stem: DeShawn picked a pair of opposite points. Find his mistake and fix it.
shown_work: Points: A at -4, B at 2, C at 4
DeShawn says: A and B are opposites, because A is negative and B is positive.
practice_problems.answer: A and C are the opposites. Opposite signs are only half the test -- the distances must match too. A is 4 units from 0 and C is 4 units from 0; B is only 2 units from 0.
practice_problems.notes: Direct bait for the canonical signs-only error.

practice_problems.stem: Point K is on the number line shown. What is the opposite of the number at Point K?
practice_problems.notes: Watch for -7 (no flip) or 0 (stops at the mirror).

practice_problems.stem: Which number is the same distance from 0 as -5, but on the other side of 0?
practice_problems.notes: No figure -- the definition in words.

practice_problems.stem: Points R and S are opposites. R is at -8. Where is S, and how far is each point from 0?
practice_problems.answer: S is at 8. Each point is 8 units from 0.
practice_problems.notes: Reverses direction -- the student produces the opposite point instead of picking it.

practice_problems.stem: Amara says 0 has no opposite. Is she right? Explain.
practice_problems.answer: No -- 0 is its own opposite. It is 0 units from 0, so its mirror image across 0 is itself.
practice_problems.notes: The standard's edge case. Accept any explanation that puts 0 at the fold point.

activities.title: Opposite Partners Match
materials: A drawn number line from -8 to 8 for checking
activities.instructions:
1. Spread all cards face up.
2. Partners take turns matching a number to its opposite and saying the two checks out loud: 'opposite sides, same distance.'
3. Every match must be proved on the number line by counting ticks from 0 both ways.
4. Two decoy cards have no partner -- finishing means explaining WHY those two are left over.

activities.title: Human Number Line Mirror
materials: Masking tape line on the floor with -8 to 8 marked
activities.instructions:
1. Lay the tape line and mark 0 with a bright card.
2. One student draws a card and stands on that number.
3. Their partner must stand on the opposite -- the group checks by counting steps from 0 on BOTH sides.
4. Trap round: teacher stands on -3 and a helper on 5. Ask: are we opposites? Why not?
5. Debrief: what two things did every correct pair have in common?

activities.title: Why Did DeShawn Pick A and B?
materials: One printed problem card per group
activities.instructions:
1. Show the group DeShawn's work and let them talk before you do.
2. Ask: what was DeShawn thinking? (His reasoning is half right -- opposites DO have opposite signs.)
3. Have the group count each point's distance from 0 and state the missing check.
4. Each student writes DeShawn a one-sentence tip.

content.worked_problem: Points: A at -4, B at 2, C at 4. DeShawn says A and B are opposites because A is negative and B is positive.
content.error_step: DeShawn checked the signs but never counted the distances from 0.
content.why: Opposites are mirror twins across 0: opposite signs AND the same distance. A and C are both 4 units from 0, so A and C are the opposites -- B is only 2 units from 0.

strategy_links.why: A concrete fold-at-0 number line makes the mirror-image meaning of 'opposite' visible before it becomes abstract.
The signs-only pairing error is a perfect find-and-fix: students must articulate the missing distance check.
Whiteboard rounds with plotted points instantly show who is pairing by sign alone.

questioning_prompts: How far is that point from 0? Count the ticks out loud.
You found two points with different signs. What ELSE has to be true before you call them opposites?
If I fold the number line at 0, which points land on each other?
Where is the opposite of 0? How do you know?

misconception_redirects.if_you_see: Student pairs any negative with any positive and calls them opposites (like -3 and 5).
misconception_redirects.say: Opposites need TWO things: opposite sides of 0 AND the same distance from 0. Count each point's ticks from 0 out loud. Do the counts match?
misconception_redirects.praise: You checked both the side and the distance. That's the whole definition of opposites.

misconception_redirects.if_you_see: Student says the opposite of the number at a point is the number itself (reads -4's opposite as -4).
misconception_redirects.say: The opposite is the point's mirror twin, not the point itself. Start at 0, count the same number of ticks in the OTHER direction, and name where you land.
misconception_redirects.praise: You crossed 0 and kept the distance -- that's a true opposite.

quick_checks.prompt: Sketch points at -6 and 4. Thumbs up or down: are they opposites?
quick_checks.look_for: An instant 'down' with 'distances don't match.' A thumbs up means the student is still pairing by signs only.

quick_checks.prompt: Point M is at -3. Say its opposite and how you know.
quick_checks.look_for: '3, because both are 3 units from 0 on opposite sides.' Answering '-3' or '0' signals the mirror idea hasn't landed.

worked_solution.stem: Point M is at -3 on the number line. What is the opposite of the number at Point M?

steps.math: Point M is at -3 -- 3 units LEFT of 0.
steps.annotation: Read the point as two pieces: distance (3) and side (left).

steps.math: Opposite = same distance, other side -> 3 units RIGHT of 0.
steps.annotation: Cross 0 and keep the distance exactly the same.
Check both tests: opposite sides of 0, and both 3 units from 0.

faded_example.stem: Point P is at 5 on the number line. What is the opposite of the number at Point P?

steps.math: Point P is at 5 -- 5 units RIGHT of 0.
steps.annotation: Distance and side are read for you.
The opposite keeps the distance but crosses 0. How far, and which side?
Name the opposite, then run both checks to prove it.

sentence_starters: The point is at ___, so its opposite is ___ -- both are ___ units from 0.
They are NOT opposites because the distances are ___ and ___.

skills.name: Name a number and its opposite from its distance from 0
skills.i_do_script: Now the picture goes away and we work from words. Watch: 'a number is 7 units to the LEFT of 0.' Distance: 7. Direction: left. Left of 0 means negative, so the number is -7 -- and its opposite is 7. The distance is always positive, but the NUMBER carries a sign. Those are two different things.

canonical_error.pattern: Writes the distance instead of the signed number -- treats 'how far from 0' and 'what number' as the same thing
canonical_error.example: For 'a number is 7 units to the left of 0,' the student writes 7 instead of -7
canonical_error.why: Distance is always positive, and the student lets that positivity leak into the number itself. This is the seed of the opposite-vs-absolute-value confusion: distance tells how far, the sign tells which side.

skills.item_template: A sentence gives a distance and direction from 0 ('N units to the left/right of 0'). Student writes the number, its opposite, or both. NR response, integers only.

sample_items.stem:
A number is 9 units to the left of 0 on a number line.

What number is it?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 9 -- the student reports the distance and drops the direction

sample_items.stem:
A number is 12 units to the right of 0 on a number line.

What is the opposite of this number?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: 12 -- the student names the number itself instead of flipping across 0

sample_items.stem:
A number is 5 units to the left of 0 on a number line.

What is the opposite of this number?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common error: -5 -- the student names the number itself; the double step (place, then flip) is skipped

sample_items.stem:
A number is 14 units to the right of 0 on a number line.

What number is it, and what is its opposite?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common errors: '14 and 14' (opposite not flipped) or '-14 and 14' (direction misread)

redirect_script.stop: Careful -- distance and number are not the same thing.
redirect_script.prompt: Underline the distance and circle the direction word. The distance tells how FAR (always positive). The direction tells the SIGN: left of 0 is negative, right of 0 is positive. Now write the number with its sign.
redirect_script.praise: You kept the distance and the sign separate. That's exactly the idea behind opposites.

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from 0 -- always counted as a positive amount.
Which way from 0 the number sits: left (negative) or right (positive).
The number at the same distance from 0 but in the other direction.

skills.manipulative_visual: Have the student physically walk it: stand at a 0 mark, take 7 steps left, and announce two things -- 'I walked 7 steps' (distance) and 'I am standing at -7' (number). The walk and the address are different.

next_steps.if_pass: Move to 6NS2-S3: write the opposite of any rational number, including decimals and fractions.
next_steps.if_fail: Return to 6NS2-S1 with the figure visible, then retry these word-only items while the student sketches a quick number line for each one.

worked_example_script.text: Write on the board: 'A number is 7 units to the left of 0 on a number line. What is the opposite of this number?'
There's no picture this time. What two pieces of information does the sentence give us about the number?
Sketch a quick number line. Start at 0 and move 7 units left. What number are you standing on?
If the student says 7, the distance has swallowed the sign. Ask: 'You WALKED 7 steps -- that's the distance. But what's the address of the spot you're standing on? Is it left or right of 0?'
Good, the number is -7. Now the question asks for its OPPOSITE. Same distance, other side -- where do you land?
So what's the final answer, and what would the answer have been if the question had only asked 'what number is it?'
Two different questions live in these problems: what's the number, and what's its opposite. Read which one is being asked before you write.
Try one alone: a number is 12 units to the right of 0. What is the opposite of this number?

printable_artifact.title: Distance vs. Number Reference Card
printable_artifact.instructions: Distance tells how far. The sign tells which side. Keep them separate.
items: Left of 0  ->  the number is negative
Right of 0  ->  the number is positive
7 units left of 0  ->  the number is -7
7 units right of 0  ->  the number is 7

practice_problems.stem: A number is 3 units to the right of 0. What number is it?
A number is 4 units to the left of 0. What number is it?
practice_problems.notes: First trap: listen for '4.'

practice_problems.stem: A number is 11 units to the left of 0 on a number line. What number is it?
A number is 8 units to the right of 0. What is the opposite of this number?
practice_problems.notes: Two moves: name the number (8), then flip it (-8). Watch for students who stop at 8.

practice_problems.stem: Maya answered a number-line question. Find her mistake and fix it.
shown_work: A number is 6 units to the left of 0. What number is it?
Maya wrote: 6, because distance is always positive.
practice_problems.answer: -6. Maya is right that the DISTANCE is positive -- it's 6 units. But the question asks for the NUMBER, and a number 6 units LEFT of 0 is -6. Distance tells how far; the sign tells which side.
practice_problems.notes: This is the opposite-vs-absolute-value confusion in its earliest form.

practice_problems.stem: A number is 5 units to the left of 0. Mark it on the number line.
Two different numbers are each 9 units from 0. What are the two numbers?
practice_problems.notes: Reverses direction: one distance, two numbers. A single answer means the left side of 0 is invisible to the student.

practice_problems.stem: The OPPOSITE of a number is 13 units to the left of 0. What is the number?
practice_problems.notes: Work backwards: the opposite is -13, so the number is 13.

activities.title: Walk the Distance, Say the Address
materials: Direction cards ('6 units left of 0', '4 units right of 0', ...)
activities.instructions:
1. A student draws a card and walks it from 0, counting steps out loud.
2. On landing they say TWO sentences: 'I walked ___ steps' and 'I am standing at ___.'
3. The group then calls out where the opposite lives, and a partner walks to it.
4. Debrief: when were the two sentences the same number, and when were they different?

activities.title: Distance or Number?
activities.instructions:
1. Read a clue aloud: 'a number is 7 units left of 0.'
2. Call either 'DISTANCE!' or 'NUMBER!' -- students write that value and hold up boards.
3. Distance answers are always positive; number answers carry the sign. Mixing them up costs the round.
4. Keep score by table. End by asking: which call was easier to get wrong, and why?

activities.title: Is Maya Right That Distance Is Always Positive?
activities.instructions:
1. Pairs read Maya's answer. First question: what did Maya get RIGHT? (Distance really is always positive.)
2. Then: what did the question actually ask for?
3. Pairs write the correct answer and one sentence Maya could use to keep distance and number separate.
4. Share out the best sentence.

content.worked_problem: A number is 6 units to the left of 0. What number is it? Maya wrote: 6, because distance is always positive.
content.error_step: Maya answered the distance question instead of the number question.
content.why: The distance from 0 is 6 units -- positive, always. But the number sitting 6 units LEFT of 0 is -6. The sign records the direction; the distance never does.

strategy_links.why: Walking the line makes distance (the walk) and the signed number (the landing spot) physically different things.
Thinking aloud -- 'distance 7, direction left, so -7' -- models the two-piece reading these word-only items need.
Maya's 'distance is always positive' error is the exact confusion to surface and fix here.

questioning_prompts: What's the distance in this sentence? What's the direction? Say both before you write.
Is the question asking for the number, or for its opposite? Point to the words that tell you.
You walked 7 steps -- that's the distance. What's the address of the spot you landed on?
How can two DIFFERENT numbers both be 9 units from 0?

misconception_redirects.if_you_see: Student writes the distance as the answer -- '7' for a number 7 units left of 0.
misconception_redirects.say: Underline the distance and circle the direction word. The distance tells how FAR (always positive). The direction tells the SIGN: left of 0 is negative, right of 0 is positive. Now write the number with its sign.
misconception_redirects.praise: You kept the distance and the sign separate. That's exactly the idea behind opposites.

misconception_redirects.if_you_see: Student answers the number itself when the question asked for its opposite (writes 12 for the opposite of a number 12 units right of 0).
misconception_redirects.say: There are two steps hiding here: first name the number, THEN flip it across 0. You did step one -- now do the flip. Same distance, other side.
misconception_redirects.praise: Two steps, done in order -- you named it and then flipped it.

steps.annotation: Flip across 0 and keep the distance: 7 units to the right.

The opposite keeps the distance of 10 but crosses to the other side of 0. Which side is that?
Write the opposite with its sign.

skills.name: Write the opposite of any rational number
skills.i_do_script: Opposites work the same for decimals and fractions as for integers: change ONLY the sign. Watch: the opposite of -3.8 is 3.8. The opposite of 5/6 is -5/6. I never touch the digits, never flip the fraction, never move the decimal point -- the number keeps its size and crosses to the other side of 0.

canonical_error.pattern: Flips the fraction (writes the reciprocal) instead of changing the sign
canonical_error.example: Says the opposite of 2/3 is 3/2 instead of -2/3
canonical_error.why: The word 'opposite' collides with 'flip it over' language students hear about reciprocals. They change the number's SIZE (turning it upside down) when opposite only ever changes the number's SIDE of 0.

skills.item_template: A single rational number (positive or negative decimal or fraction). Student writes its opposite. NR response. No computation beyond changing the sign.

sample_items.stem: What is the opposite of -3.8?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common errors: -3.8 (no flip), 8.3 (digits reversed), 3.08 (decimal moved)

sample_items.stem: What is the opposite of 5/6?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common errors: 6/5 (reciprocal -- the canonical trap), -6/5 (reciprocal plus sign), 5/6 (no change)

sample_items.stem: What is the opposite of 12.4?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common errors: 12.4 (no change), 4.21 (digits shuffled), -4.12 (digits shuffled with sign)

sample_items.stem: What is the opposite of -2/5?
sample_items.distractor_logic: Common errors: -5/2 (reciprocal, sign kept), 5/2 (reciprocal with sign change), -2/5 (no change)

redirect_script.stop: Stop -- did the digits change, or just the sign?
redirect_script.prompt: The opposite changes ONE thing: the sign. Cover the sign with your finger -- everything you can still see must stay exactly the same. Now write the number with the other sign.
redirect_script.praise: Same digits, opposite sign. You didn't let 'opposite' turn into 'flip the fraction.'

vocabulary.definition: Any number that can be written as a fraction -- integers, decimals like 3.8, and fractions like 5/6.
The same number on the other side of 0 -- only the sign changes.
A fraction flipped upside down (2/3 becomes 3/2). This is NOT the opposite -- it changes the size, not the side.

skills.manipulative_visual: Write the number on a card in two parts: the sign on a small sticky note and the digits on the card. Taking the opposite = swapping only the sticky note. The card itself never changes.

next_steps.if_pass: Move to 6NS2-S4: explain in words where a number and its opposite sit on the number line.
next_steps.if_fail: Drop back to 6NS2-S2 with integers only, then reintroduce decimals first (they feel more like integers) and fractions last.

worked_example_script.text: Write two problems side by side: 'What is the opposite of -3.8?' and 'What is the opposite of 5/6?'
Before we touch these -- what did 'opposite' mean for integers? What changed, and what stayed the same?
Where does -3.8 live on a number line -- which side of 0, roughly how far? So where does its opposite live?
Write the opposite of -3.8. Did any digit change? Did the decimal point move?
Now 5/6. Some students write 6/5. What did they change about the number -- its sign, or its size?
If the student writes 6/5, they've reached for the reciprocal. Ask: 'Is 6/5 on the other side of 0 from 5/6? Both are positive! Which side of 0 should the opposite of a positive number be on?'
So what IS the opposite of 5/6? Say what changed and what stayed.
One rule for every rational number: the opposite keeps the digits and crosses 0. Flipping a fraction is a different move with a different name -- reciprocal -- and it belongs to a different job.

printable_artifact.title: Opposite vs. Reciprocal Reference Card
printable_artifact.instructions: Opposite changes the SIGN. Reciprocal changes the SIZE. Never both jobs at once.
items: Digits never change. Decimal never moves.
Opposite = same distance, other side of 0

activities.title: Find My Opposite (Reciprocal Decoys)
activities.instructions:
1. Spread the cards face up.
2. Partners match each number to its OPPOSITE, saying 'same digits, other sign' for every match.
3. Three decoy cards are reciprocals -- they match nothing.
4. Finish by explaining what job the leftover cards actually do (they're reciprocals, not opposites).

activities.title: Sign Flip Speed Round
activities.instructions:
1. Flash a rational number (mix integers, decimals, fractions): -4, 2.9, -5/8, 7/10, -0.3.
2. Students write the opposite and hold up boards on 'show.'
3. Any board showing a flipped fraction gets the class question: 'sign change or size change?'
4. Speed up as accuracy holds. End with the trap: 'opposite of 0?' (0 -- its own opposite).

activities.title: Leo's Flip
activities.instructions:
1. Show Leo's work. Ask first: where might Leo have heard 'flip' before? (Reciprocals -- his memory is real, just misfiled.)
2. Have the group place 4/9, 9/4, and -4/9 roughly on a number line.
3. Ask: which one is the mirror twin of 4/9 across 0?
4. Each student writes one sentence telling opposite and reciprocal apart.

content.worked_problem: What is the opposite of 4/9? Leo wrote: 9/4 -- you flip the fraction to get the opposite.
content.error_step: Leo flipped the fraction (reciprocal) instead of flipping the sign.
content.why: The opposite of 4/9 is -4/9: same digits, same distance from 0, opposite side. 9/4 is a bigger number on the SAME side of 0 -- it can't be the opposite.

strategy_links.why: Rapid choral sign-flips build the 'change only the sign' reflex across integers, decimals, and fractions.
The reciprocal-for-opposite error is this skill's signature bug -- analyzing it head-on separates the two moves.
Whiteboard rounds expose instantly whose fractions are flipping upside down instead of changing sign.

questioning_prompts: What is the ONLY thing allowed to change when you take an opposite?
Are 5/6 and 6/5 on opposite sides of 0? So can they be opposites?
Where is -3.8 on the number line? Where must its opposite be?
How far from 0 is -2/5? How far from 0 is its opposite?

misconception_redirects.praise: Same digits, opposite sign. You didn't let 'opposite' turn into 'flip the fraction.'

misconception_redirects.if_you_see: Student leaves a negative number negative (says the opposite of -3.8 is -3.8) because 'it already has a sign.'

misconception_redirects.praise: You crossed 0 -- negative numbers get positive opposites, every time.

quick_checks.look_for: 'True' with a number-line reason. Hesitation means the student still sees the sign as a fixed label.

skills.name: Explain where a number and its opposite sit on the number line
skills.i_do_script: Now we put the idea into words. Watch me describe -9 and 9: '9 is 9 units to the RIGHT of 0. -9 is 9 units to the LEFT of 0. Both are 9 units from 0, in opposite directions.' Three sentences, and notice -- the DISTANCE is the same in all of them. The negative sign never makes a number closer to or farther from 0.

canonical_error.pattern: Believes the negative number in an opposite pair is closer to 0 because it is 'smaller'
canonical_error.example: Says -9 is closer to 0 than 9 because -9 is less than 9
canonical_error.why: The student conflates a number's VALUE with its DISTANCE from 0. -9 is indeed less than 9, but distance ignores direction -- both are exactly 9 units from 0. This is the opposite-vs-absolute-value confusion.

skills.item_template: A pair of opposites (-N and N). Student selects the three true statements about their locations from six choices, or explains the locations in words. MS with 6 choices.

sample_items.stem: Select the three statements that correctly explain the locations of -15 and 15 on a number line.

sample_items.distractor_logic: Direction-swapped statements test left/right of 0; '-15 is closer to 0' baits the belief that a negative number's size shrinks its distance from 0.

redirect_script.stop: Hmm -- is 'less than' the same as 'closer to 0'?
redirect_script.prompt: Count -9's ticks from 0. Now count 9's ticks from 0. Write both counts down. Are they the same or different? Value tells which number is less; distance tells how far from 0 -- they're different questions.
redirect_script.praise: You separated value from distance. Opposites are ALWAYS the same distance from 0.

vocabulary.definition: One number left of 0 and the other right of 0.
How many units away from 0 -- direction doesn't count.
How big or small a number is on the number line. -9 has a LESSER value than 9, but the SAME distance from 0.

worked_example_script.text: Write -9 and 9 on the board with a number line underneath, both points plotted.
Which of these two numbers is LESS? How do you know from the number line?
Different question now: which of the two is CLOSER to 0? Count each one's ticks from 0.
If the student says -9 is closer 'because it's smaller,' they've merged value with distance. Have them physically count ticks both ways from 0 and write the two counts side by side.
So what's the same about -9 and 9, and what's different? Try to say it in one sentence each.
Write the three-sentence frame: '9 is __ units to the __ of 0. -9 is __ units to the __ of 0. Both are __ units from 0, in __ directions.'
Fill in the frame for -9 and 9. Which blanks got the SAME number?
Now say the frame for -25 and 25 without the number line. Which parts changed, and which parts never change for ANY opposite pair?

practice_problems.stem: Select the three statements that correctly explain the locations of -12 and 12 on a number line: (a) 12 is 12 units right of 0; (b) -12 is 12 units right of 0; (c) -12 is 12 units left of 0; (d) -12 is closer to 0 than 12; (e) both numbers are 12 units from 0, in opposite directions; (f) 12 is 12 units left of 0.

practice_problems.stem: Jordan compared an opposite pair. Find the mistake and fix it.

2. Partners take turns reading a statement aloud and placing it -- the other partner must agree or challenge.
3. Every False card must be FIXED out loud: say the corrected statement.
4. Debrief question: which false card fooled you longest, and what made it convincing?

materials: Two same-length paper strips per group

1. Show Jordan's claim. First ask: what is Jordan RIGHT about? (-12 really is less than 12.)
2. Anchor both paper strips at 0 on a drawn line -- stretch one to -12, one to 12. Compare lengths.

Jordan's 'smaller means closer' claim is the exact misconception this skill exists to dismantle.

steps.annotation: Positive numbers live right of 0; the distance is the number's size.
The sign flips the direction, not the distance.

skills.name: Reason about the opposite of the opposite of a number
skills.i_do_script: Taking an opposite is a FLIP across 0. Watch what two flips do to -4: the opposite of -4 is 4 -- that's flip one. The opposite of 4 is -4 -- flip two, and I'm back where I started. So -(-4) means 'the opposite of -4,' which is 4 -- one flip. Every extra opposite is one more flip, and two flips always bring a number home.

canonical_error.pattern: Reads -(-a) as 'still negative' -- treats each negative sign as a label meaning 'negative' instead of a flip across 0
canonical_error.example: Says -(-4) = -4, or says the opposite of the opposite of 7 is -7
canonical_error.why: The student sees a negative sign anywhere and concludes the answer is negative. They aren't tracking that each opposite is an ACTION (a flip across 0), so two flips cancel and return the original number.

skills.item_template: A nested-opposite prompt: -(-n) notation, 'the opposite of the opposite of' language (with numbers or a variable), or a real-world flip. MC with 4 choices.

sample_items.stem: If n is a positive number, what is the opposite of the opposite of -n?
choices: -n
n
2n
sample_items.distractor_logic: n comes from counting only one flip; 0 treats the flips as cancelling to nothing; 2n confuses opposite with doubling the distance.

sample_items.stem: What is the value of -(-9)?
sample_items.distractor_logic: -9 is the canonical 'a negative sign means the answer is negative' error; 0 treats the signs as wiping the number out; 18 doubles instead of flipping.

sample_items.stem: If x = 12, what is the value of the opposite of the opposite of x?
sample_items.distractor_logic: -12 counts only one flip; 0 and 24 come from cancel-to-nothing and doubling misreads.

sample_items.stem: A submarine is at -250 feet (below sea level). It rises to the opposite position. What is its new position?
choices: 250 feet above sea level
250 feet below sea level
0 feet (sea level)
500 feet below sea level
sample_items.distractor_logic: 250 below keeps the sign (no flip); 0 stops at the mirror line; 500 below doubles the depth instead of crossing 0.

redirect_script.stop: Hold on -- how many flips are in this problem?
redirect_script.prompt: Each 'opposite' (each - sign in front) is one FLIP across 0. Draw the hops: start at the number, flip once, flip again if there's a second sign. Where did you land?
redirect_script.praise: You counted the flips instead of just spotting a negative sign. That's the reasoning.

vocabulary.definition: Flipping across 0 twice -- which lands you back on the number you started with.
One trip across 0 to the mirror point on the other side. Each - sign in front of a number is one flip.
A letter like n that stands for a number. -n means 'the opposite of n,' whatever n is.

skills.manipulative_visual: Draw hop arrows over a number line: start at -4, one arc over 0 landing on 4 (flip one), a second arc back to -4 (flip two). The arcs make 'two flips come home' visible.

next_steps.if_pass: Ready for 6.NS.3 territory: absolute value as distance from 0, and ordering rational numbers.
next_steps.if_fail: Drop back to 6NS2-S3 for single opposites, then rebuild this skill with hop arrows on a drawn line -- one arc per sign -- before returning to -(-n) notation.

worked_example_script.text: Write on the board: -(-4). Underneath, draw a number line from -5 to 5.
Read this out loud with me: 'the opposite of negative four.' How many 'opposite' moves do you see written down?
Where does -4 live on our line? Put your finger on it.
Now do one flip: the opposite of -4. Same distance, other side of 0 -- where do you land?

If the student says -(-4) is -4 'because there's a negative sign,' they're reading signs as labels, not flips. Have them draw one hop arc from -4 over 0 and name the landing spot before any talk of signs.
So -(-4) = 4. New question: what is the opposite of the OPPOSITE of -4 -- two flips this time. Flip from -4, then flip again. Where are you?
Back at -4! Why do two flips always land you where you started, no matter what number you begin with?
That's the rule the standard wants you to own: the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself. Signs aren't decorations -- each one is a flip, and two flips come home.

printable_artifact.title: Count the Flips Reference Card
printable_artifact.instructions: Each - sign in front is one flip across 0. Count flips -- don't just spot signs.
items: Two flips: opposite of the opposite of 7  ->  7
Two flips: opposite of the opposite of -n  ->  -n
Even number of flips  ->  back to the start
Odd number of flips  ->  the opposite
0 flips nowhere: the opposite of 0 is 0

practice_problems.stem: What is the opposite of -8?
What is the opposite of the opposite of 5?
practice_problems.notes: Two flips in words before any -(-n) notation appears.

practice_problems.stem: What is the value of -(-15)?
practice_problems.notes: Watch for -15 -- the 'a negative sign means negative' reflex.

practice_problems.stem: Tanya evaluated an expression. Find her mistake and fix it.
shown_work: Tanya wrote: There is a negative sign, so the answer stays negative. -(-6) = -6.
practice_problems.answer: 6. -(-6) means 'the opposite of -6.' One flip across 0 takes -6 to 6. Tanya treated the sign as a label meaning 'negative' instead of as a flip -- count the flips, don't just spot the sign.
practice_problems.notes: The canonical -(-4) = -4 double-opposite bait with fresh numbers.

practice_problems.stem: If p is a positive number, what is the opposite of the opposite of -p?
practice_problems.notes: Two flips starting from -p land back on -p. Watch for p (one flip counted).

practice_problems.stem: Start at -3. Take the opposite, then take the opposite of the result. Mark where you end on the number line.
practice_problems.notes: The two hops should be visible in the student's pencil work: -3 to 3, then back to -3.

practice_problems.stem: What is the value of -(-(-9))?
practice_problems.notes: Three signs total around the 9: innermost number is -9, flip 1 gives 9, flip 2 gives -9. An even number of OUTER flips returns the start; here the two outer signs bring -9 home.

practice_problems.stem: Explain why the opposite of the opposite of ANY number is the number itself.
practice_problems.answer: Taking an opposite flips a number to the other side of 0 at the same distance. Flipping twice crosses 0 and crosses back, so the number returns to exactly where it started.
practice_problems.notes: Explain-why stretch -- the standard's own sentence, in the student's words.

activities.title: Two Flips on the Line
activities.instructions:
1. A student stands on a starting number (say -4) and announces it.
2. Each time a 'OPPOSITE!' card is flipped, the student must walk to the mirror spot across 0 -- the group counts the units aloud both ways to check.
3. Run one flip, then two flips, then three. After each run, ask: where did you end compared to where you started?
4. Debrief: what do even numbers of flips always do? Odd numbers?

activities.title: Tanya's Sticky Sign
activities.instructions:
1. Pairs read Tanya's reasoning. Ask first: why is her rule tempting? (Negative signs usually DO make things negative.)
2. Have pairs draw the hop arc for -(-6) on a small number line: start at -6, one flip.
3. Ask: how many flips does -(-6) contain? Where does one flip from -6 land?
4. Pairs write Tanya a one-sentence rule that beats 'stays negative.'

content.worked_problem: Evaluate -(-6). Tanya wrote: there is a negative sign, so the answer stays negative. -(-6) = -6.
content.error_step: Tanya read the outer - sign as a label ('the answer is negative') instead of as an action (flip across 0).
content.why: -(-6) means the opposite of -6. One flip across 0 takes -6 to 6. Each - sign in front is one flip -- count the flips, don't just spot a sign.

activities.title: Flip Counter Showdown
activities.instructions:
1. Write a nested expression on the board: -(-7), the opposite of the opposite of 3, -(-(-2)).
2. Students write TWO things: the number of flips, and the final answer.
3. On 'show,' a right flip-count with a wrong answer scores half -- the count is the thinking.
4. Final round with a variable: the opposite of the opposite of -n. Debrief why the answer keeps its letter.

strategy_links.why: Pairing a correct two-flip worked example against Tanya's 'stays negative' work makes the flip-versus-label contrast explicit.
Narrating 'flip one lands here, flip two lands here' aloud models the action-tracking this skill demands.
Hop arcs on a drawn line give a concrete representation of nesting before the -(-n) notation stands alone.

questioning_prompts: How many flips are written in this expression? Count the signs in front, not the sign inside the number.
Where does one flip from -6 land? Where does the second flip land?
Why do two flips always bring you back to the start, no matter the number?
If n could be ANY number, what is the opposite of the opposite of n? How do you know without picking a number?

misconception_redirects.if_you_see: Student sees -(-6) and answers -6 because 'there's a negative sign, so it stays negative.'
misconception_redirects.say: Each 'opposite' (each - sign in front) is one FLIP across 0. Draw the hops: start at the number, flip once, flip again if there's a second sign. Where did you land?
misconception_redirects.praise: You counted the flips instead of just spotting a negative sign. That's the reasoning.

misconception_redirects.if_you_see: Student answers 0 for a double opposite, saying the two signs 'cancel out to nothing.'
misconception_redirects.say: The flips cancel each other, but the NUMBER never disappears. Start at 7 on the line, flip twice, and tell me the spot you're standing on -- is it 0?
misconception_redirects.praise: Right -- the flips undo each other and the number comes home, full size.

quick_checks.look_for: 'One flip in front, answer 11.' An answer of -11 means signs are still labels; 0 means 'cancel' is being misread as 'vanish.'

quick_checks.prompt: The opposite of the opposite of -5 -- what is it, and why?
quick_checks.look_for: '-5, because two flips bring it back.' Answering 5 means the student counted one flip and stopped.

worked_solution.stem: What is the opposite of the opposite of -4?

steps.annotation: Put your finger on -4: 4 units left of 0.
One flip across 0 -- same distance, right side.
The second flip crosses back. Two flips always come home.

steps.math: The opposite of the opposite of -4 is -4.
steps.annotation: The number itself -- exactly what the standard says.
Read the outer sign as an action, not a label.
-12 is 12 units left of 0. One flip lands the same distance on the other side. Where?
Write the value. Check: did you count one flip or two?

diagnostic_flow.description: Start with S3 (write the opposite of any rational number) — the heart of the standard. If they pass, move to S5 (opposite of the opposite). If they fail, check whether the gap is S1 (seeing opposites on the line) or S2 (distance vs. signed number). S4 (explaining locations) is the branch check when mechanics pass but reasoning wobbles.
